lead.title: Perfuze wins FDA clearance for NeuroSheath, completing its stroke thrombectomy system
lead.deck: The Galway medtech announced on Nov. 17 510(k) clearance for NeuroSheath, an 8F long sheath for neurovascular access sized for its Millipede88 super-bore aspiration catheter, which was cleared in March for standalone direct aspiration; a limited market release is starting at select U.S. stroke centers ahead of a full launch in 2027. With access and aspiration now under one brand, the Irish startup is no longer selling a catheter but a system, which changes its standing against the thrombectomy giants and makes it a natural target.

milestone.title: Stockholm startup Sine Health secures the first 510(k) for essential tremor monitoring using only a smartphone
milestone.summary: Cleared under K261026, Sine passively measures tremor with the phone's own sensors, running in the background, and gives the neurologist an objective view of how it evolves between visits. It is the company's second FDA clearance (formerly Nordic Kinetics), after an Apple Watch-based Parkinson's monitoring system in June, even though it was only founded last year.
milestone.why: Essential tremor affects about 7 million Americans and is still judged on a few minutes of in-clinic observation; continuous measurement becomes valuable as new therapies (drugs, focused ultrasound, neurostimulation) arrive and must prove their real-world effect. Two FDA clearances in a year for such a young European company: a profile to track ahead of its next round.

deal.thesis: HealthQuest Capital leads this oversubscribed round, with Braidwell and Olympus Innovation Ventures joining Sofinnova Partners, Norwest and Perceptive, to accelerate commercialization of the Aliya pulsed electric field (PEF) soft-tissue ablation platform and advance RheOx in chronic bronchitis, already launched in Europe in 2022. The thesis: electroporation, which conquered atrial fibrillation, can become a general ablation modality in oncology and pulmonology, and Olympus joining the cap table sketches a natural acquirer.

brefsEurope.title: Basel neurotech Indivi acquires Cogitat, the Imperial College spin-out, and its EEG foundation model
brefsEurope.summary: Announced on Nov. 17 with undisclosed terms, the deal brings NeuroRVQ, an AI model that decodes cognitive activity from EEG across any patient or headset, and Cogitat's team, which will keep developing it. Indivi, which already runs smartphone-based motor and cognitive assessments in Parkinson's, MS and Alzheimer's, wants to detect disease and treatment effects earlier for pharma trials.

brefsEurope.title: EIC Accelerator picks French startups EndoGene.Bio and Surgecare among its 35 winners
brefsEurope.summary: Published on Nov. 16, the selection (35 companies out of 453 proposals, €84M in proposed grants and up to €10M of equity each via the EIC Fund) includes EndoGene.Bio and its uterine disease stratification engine based on menstrual blood analysis, and Surgecare, whose PreCyte test aims to support day-1 discharge decisions after abdominal surgery. France is among the three best-represented countries.

brefsEurope.title: Werfen wins FDA clearance for the ROTEM sigma complete cartridge in trauma bleeding
brefsEurope.summary: Announced on Nov. 17, the expanded indication lets this viscoelastic test be used at the point of care or in the lab to assess bleeding and thrombosis in adult trauma patients, beyond cardiac surgery and liver transplantation. The Catalan diagnostics group is targeting trauma-induced coagulopathy, where guidelines already recommend this type of testing.

brefsEurope.title: MHRA launches a Women's Health Programme to bring more women into drug and device trials
brefsEurope.summary: Unveiled at the DIA-MHRA summit on Nov. 16-17, the programme starts from a hard number: of 4,616 UK trial applications from 2019 to 2023, pregnant women were included in just 1.1%. A signal for UK femtech (nearly £300M in annual turnover), whose regulatory framework is struggling to keep pace with software tools.

brefsIntl.title: Medtronic expands FDA clearance of its Hugo robot to general surgery
brefsIntl.summary: The expanded 510(k) announced on Nov. 17 covers all upper abdominal general surgery (cholecystectomy, gastric bypass, ventral hernia…), inguinal hernia and appendectomy, about 3.5 million U.S. procedures a year. Key comparable: in the U.S., Hugo moves beyond urology into the core of Intuitive's market, raising the bar for European challengers CMR Surgical, Distalmotion and Moon Surgical.

brefsIntl.title: Newton wins MDR CE mark for Neurolens N3, its ocular misalignment measurement system
brefsIntl.summary: Issued by Intertek Medical Notified Body and announced on Nov. 17, the certificate covers the eye-tracking device that measures eye alignment at distance and near to prescribe prism lenses against headaches and eye strain. Launch in the first European markets is planned for 2027.

brefsIntl.title: KKR completes its $5.7B buyout of Integer, taking one of medtech's largest contract manufacturers private
brefsIntl.summary: The contract maker of cardiovascular, neuromodulation and cardiac rhythm devices, the world's 56th-largest medtech group, leaves the NYSE at $127 a share. Market comparable: private equity is paying up for the catheter and implant manufacturing capacity that startups depend on.

word.definition: A procedure in which a catheter is threaded from an artery in the groin or wrist up to the brain to suck out or grab the clot blocking a large artery during a stroke, restoring blood flow before the brain tissue dies.

parts.label: Sheath and access catheter
parts.role: the road: they travel from the femoral or radial artery up to the carotids and stabilize the whole setup

parts.label: Aspiration catheter
parts.role: the vacuum: a large-bore tube placed against the clot to aspirate it in one piece

parts.label: Stent retriever
parts.role: the net: a metal mesh deployed inside the clot to trap it and pull it out

how.t: CT or MRI confirms a large vessel occlusion and, beyond the first hours, that salvageable tissue (penumbra) remains.
Under X-ray, the neurointerventionalist advances the sheath, access catheter and then the aspiration catheter up to the clot.
The clot is aspirated or pulled out with the stent retriever; the result is graded on the TICI scale, with near-complete reperfusion on the first pass as the goal.

word.why: Since the DAWN and DEFUSE-3 trials, thrombectomy can benefit selected patients up to 24 hours after symptom onset: the market has grown far faster than the number of operators. Startups now compete on first-pass success (0.088-inch super-bore catheters, funnels, retrievers for small distal arteries) and on system simplicity, hence a string of clearances (Perfuze, Route 92) and sizable rounds (Anaconda, $56M). The giants (Stryker, Medtronic, Penumbra, J&J) remain the natural acquirers.

startups.name: Perfuze
startups.use: Millipede88 super-bore aspiration catheter FDA-cleared for standalone direct aspiration (March 2026), completed in November by the NeuroSheath 8F sheath

startups.name: Anaconda Biomed
startups.use: Funnel thrombectomy catheters (ANA) and CONDA stent retriever; $56M raise to complete the U.S. ATHENA pivotal trial

startups.name: Rapid Medical
startups.use: Adjustable Tigertriever stent retrievers; Tigertriever 25 FDA-cleared in April 2026 and Tigertriever 13 tested in distal occlusions (DISTALS trial)

startups.name: Route 92 Medical
startups.use: 0.088-inch HiPoint aspiration system backed by the SUMMIT MAX randomized trial; $50M growth round led by Novo Holdings in 2026
